subject.title: fix(scripts): warn when postinstall detects running gateway with stale module imports

question: After the opt-out compatibility bug is fixed, should OpenClaw accept a postinstall loopback probe plus OPENCLAW_DISABLE_POSTINSTALL_RESTART_WARNING as an advisory stale-gateway mitigation?
rationale: The compatibility fix is mechanical, but install-time probing, a new environment surface, and overlap with the update-CLI warning PR are operator-experience choices that automation should not settle alone.

options.title: Accept After Opt-Out Fix
options.body: Fix the existing disable-flag regression, then treat this PR as a warning-only postinstall mitigation while keeping the stale-gateway issue open.

options.title: Require Packaged Gateway Proof
options.body: Ask for redacted output from a real package update or rollback with an already-running gateway before accepting the postinstall probe.

options.title: Pause For One Recovery Layer
options.body: Hold or close this PR if maintainers want the update CLI or runtime stale-import handling to be the only warning and recovery boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept After Opt-Out Fix
recommendation.body: Fix the existing disable-flag regression, then treat this PR as a warning-only postinstall mitigation while keeping the stale-gateway issue open.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans postinstall behavior, package update UX, and gateway restart policy where this person has strong historical path signal.
